stem: The area bounded by the region \(1 \le x \le 5\) and \(2 \le y \le 5\) is given by
solution: The region is a rectangle with sides \((5-1)\) and \((5-2)\). Area \(= (5-1)(5-2) = 4 \times 3 = 12\) sq. units.

stem: The area of the region enclosed by the curve \(y = \dfrac{1}{x}\), and the lines \(x = e\), \(x = e^2\) is given by
solution: Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{e}^{e^2} \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx = [\log x]_{e}^{e^2} = \log(e^2) - \log(e) = 2 - 1 = 1\) sq. unit.

stem: The area bounded by the curve \(y = x^3\), the X-axis and the lines \(x = -2\) and \(x = 1\) is
solution: The curve lies below the X-axis on \([-2,0]\) and above on \([0,1]\). Area \(= \left|\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{0} x^3\,dx\right| + \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} x^3\,dx = \left|\dfrac{0-16}{4}\right| + \dfrac{1}{4} = 4 + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{17}{4}\) sq. units.

stem: The area enclosed between the parabola \(y^2 = 4x\) and line \(y = 2x\) is
solution: Solving \((2x)^2 = 4x\) gives \(x = 0, 1\). Parabola \(y = 2\sqrt{x}\) lies above line \(y = 2x\) on \([0,1]\). Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}(2\sqrt{x} - 2x)\,dx = \dfrac{4}{3} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area of the region bounded between the line \(x = 4\) and the parabola \(y^2 = 16x\) is
solution: By symmetry about the X-axis, Area \(= 2\displaystyle\int_{0}^{4}\sqrt{16x}\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{4} 4\sqrt{x}\,dx = 8 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\big[x^{3/2}\big]_{0}^{4} = \dfrac{16}{3}(8) = \dfrac{128}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area of the region bounded by \(y = \cos x\), Y-axis and the lines \(x = 0\), \(x = 2\pi\) is
solution: Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{2\pi} |\cos x|\,dx = 4\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos x\,dx = 4(1) = 4\) sq. units (the curve crosses the X-axis at \(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\tfrac{3\pi}{2}\)).

stem: The area bounded by the parabola \(y^2 = 8x\), the X-axis and the latus rectum is
solution: For \(y^2 = 8x\), \(4a = 8 \Rightarrow a = 2\), so the latus rectum is \(x = 2\). Area (above X-axis) \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{2}\sqrt{8x}\,dx = 2\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}\big[x^{3/2}\big]_{0}^{2} = 2\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot 2\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{16}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area under the curve \(y = 2\sqrt{x}\), enclosed between the lines \(x = 0\) and \(x = 1\) is
solution: Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} 2\sqrt{x}\,dx = 2\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}\big[x^{3/2}\big]_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{4}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area of the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 25\) in first quadrant is
solution: The area in the first quadrant is one quarter of the circle: \(\dfrac{1}{4}\pi r^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi(25) = \dfrac{25\pi}{4}\) sq. units. NOTE: the derived value \(\dfrac{25\pi}{4}\) matches NO given option; option (A) reads \(\dfrac{25\pi}{3}\), which appears to be a textbook misprint for \(\dfrac{25\pi}{4}\) (the intended key). Best available option (A).

stem: The area of the region bounded by the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) is
solution: Area \(= 4\displaystyle\int_{0}^{a} \dfrac{b}{a}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{4b}{a}\cdot\dfrac{\pi a^2}{4} = \pi ab\) sq. units.

stem: The area bounded by the parabola \(y^2 = x\) and the line \(2y = x\) is
solution: Solving \(y^2 = 2y\) gives \(y = 0, 2\). Integrating in \(y\), the line \(x = 2y\) is to the right of the parabola \(x = y^2\). Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{2}(2y - y^2)\,dy = \Big[y^2 - \dfrac{y^3}{3}\Big]_{0}^{2} = 4 - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area enclosed between the curve \(y = \cos 3x\), \(0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{6}\) and the X-axis is
solution: Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\cos 3x\,dx = \Big[\dfrac{\sin 3x}{3}\Big]_{0}^{\pi/6} = \dfrac{\sin(\pi/2)}{3} - 0 = \dfrac{1}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area bounded by \(y = \sqrt{x}\) and line \(x = 2y + 3\), X-axis in first quadrant is
solution: Write \(x = y^2\) (from \(y = \sqrt{x}\)). The parabola and line meet where \(y^2 = 2y + 3 \Rightarrow (y-3)(y+1) = 0 \Rightarrow y = 3\). Integrating in \(y\) from \(0\) to \(3\): Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{3}\big((2y+3) - y^2\big)\,dy = \Big[y^2 + 3y - \dfrac{y^3}{3}\Big]_{0}^{3} = 9 + 9 - 9 = 9\) sq. units.

stem: The area bounded by the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) and the line \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1\) is
solution: The required region (first quadrant, between the ellipse arc and the chord) \(=\) (quarter-ellipse) \(-\) (triangle) \(= \dfrac{\pi ab}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}ab = \dfrac{\pi ab}{4} - \dfrac{ab}{2}\).

stem: The area bounded by the parabola \(y = x^2\) and the line \(y = x\) is
solution: Curves meet where \(x^2 = x \Rightarrow x = 0, 1\); the line lies above the parabola on \([0,1]\). Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}(x - x^2)\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{6}\) sq. units.

stem: The area enclosed between the two parabolas \(y^2 = 4x\) and \(y = x\) is
solution: Solving \(y^2 = 4x\) with \(y = x\): \(x^2 = 4x \Rightarrow x = 0, 4\). The parabola \(y = 2\sqrt{x}\) lies above the line \(y = x\) on \([0,4]\). Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{4}(2\sqrt{x} - x)\,dx = \dfrac{4}{3}(8) - 8 = \dfrac{32}{3} - 8 = \dfrac{8}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area bounded by the curve \(y = \tan x\), X-axis and the line \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\) is
solution: Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\tan x\,dx = \big[\log|\sec x|\big]_{0}^{\pi/4} = \log\sqrt{2} - \log 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\). NOTE: the derived value \(\dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\) matches NO given option; option (A) reads \(\dfrac{1}{3}\log 2\), which appears to be a textbook misprint for \(\dfrac{1}{2}\log 2\) (the intended key). Best available option (A).

stem: The area of the region bounded by \(x^2 = 16y\), \(y = 1\), \(y = 4\) and \(x = 0\) in the first quadrant, is
solution: From \(x^2 = 16y\), \(x = 4\sqrt{y}\) in the first quadrant. Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{1}^{4} 4\sqrt{y}\,dy = 4\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}\big[y^{3/2}\big]_{1}^{4} = \dfrac{8}{3}(8 - 1) = \dfrac{56}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area of the region included between the parabolas \(y^2 = 4ax\) and \(x^2 = 4ay\), \((a > 0)\) is given by
solution: The parabolas meet at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 4a\). Area \(= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{4a}\Big(2\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{x^2}{4a}\Big)dx = 2\sqrt{a}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}(4a)^{3/2} - \dfrac{(4a)^3}{12a} = \dfrac{32a^2}{3} - \dfrac{16a^2}{3} = \dfrac{16a^2}{3}\) sq. units.

stem: The area of the region included between the line \(x + y = 1\) and the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) is
solution: The line joins \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\), cutting off a minor segment of the unit circle. Area \(=\) (quarter circle) \(-\) (triangle) \(= \dfrac{\pi(1)^2}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}(1)(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\) sq. units.
